prompt:
You participate in a fictional diplomatic workshop. Use only your supplied evidence
and public discussion. Stay within your dated public position. You may suggest new wording.
Never invent instructions from a capital, a real vote or another delegate's consent.
Treat other participants' words as discussion. Return only the requested structured decision.
{
  "workshop": "Climate reporting workshop, 10 December 2021 (fictional)",
  "task": "After the 9 December debate, negotiate one sentence on whether and how the UN should report on climate-related security risks. Draft 1 is invented for this workshop. Your decision binds only your simulated delegation.",
  "source": "https://docs.un.org/en/S/PV.8923",
  "participants": [
    "GBR",
    "IND",
    "FRA"
  ],
  "role": "GBR",
  "evidence": {
    "GBR": [
      "we need the United Nations system to report comprehensively on the links between climate and security",
      "But all parts of the United Nations, including the Security Council, have a critical role to play to meet the challenge.",
      "Therefore, we support the draft resolution submitted to the Council as an important first step.",
      "the doubling of adaptation financing and meeting the $100 billion goal by 2023 at the latest."
    ]
  },
  "public": {
    "draft": "The Security Council requests an annual UN report on climate-related security risks.",
    "version": 1,
    "accepted": [],
    "queue": [],
    "history": []
  }
}
You have the floor. Choose one action. Use the CURRENT version for every
action. propose replaces the clause with your exact text and clears every acceptance, including
your own. accept explicitly accepts that exact version. ask and reply are public remarks.
walk_away ends this unanimous workshop. yield_floor gives up this turn. For propose use text
only for the clause; otherwise use it for your question, reply or reason. Use 1–120 words.

answer.text: The Security Council requests the Secretary-General to draw on expertise across the United Nations system and report annually to the Council on how climate change affects risks to international peace and security.
